source_identity.canonical_title: Une inégalité n'est pas forcément injuste, inégalité n'est pas synonyme d'injustice

translation.canonical_title: Inequality is not necessarily unfair and is not synonymous with injustice
translation.displayed_title: Inequality is not necessarily unfair and is not synonymous with injustice
translation.summary: An inequality can be justified. The fact that women are, on average, physically weaker than men is an inequality, but it is not unfair. The fact that people who work part-time earn less money is unequal, but not unfair. The fact that many more women than men work part-time is unequal, but not unfair. The fact that people who work at night are paid more is unequal, but not unfair. The fact that most people who work at night are men is unequal, but not unfair. The fact that most skilled construction workers are men, or that most home care workers are women, is unequal, but not unfair. The fact that women have longer hair than men on average is unequal, but not unfair. The fact that women wear high-heeled shoes or makeup more often than men on average is unequal, but not unfair.
